title: All Four Operations with Signed Numbers
short: Solve problems with all four operations on rational numbers.
trouble: Students apply the wrong sign rule when operations are mixed, such as treating −2 − 3 as a product.

blocks.html: Now you can add and subtract and multiply and divide signed numbers. Real problems mix all four, so two old ideas come back: the order of operations, and choosing the right sign rule for each step.
Work in order: parentheses, exponents, multiply and divide (left to right), add and subtract (left to right). At each step, use the sign rule for that operation.

Each operation keeps its own meaning. In $-2 - 3$, the 3 is subtracted: a move of 3 to the left, ending at $-5$. In $(-2)(-3)$, two negatives are multiplied, and the product is $6$. Mixing them up changes the problem. Doing one step at a time keeps each meaning clear.

blocks.name: integerline
blocks.cap: $-2 - 3$ is a subtraction: from $-2$, move 3 to the left. It lands on $-5$, not on a positive number.

blocks.title: Parentheses first
steps: The fraction bar groups the top: $-6 + 2 = -4$.

blocks.title: A diver
blocks.q: A diver is at $-12$ m. She swims down 3 m per minute for 4 minutes, then up 5 m. Where does she end?
steps: Add left to right: $-12 + (-12) = -24$, then $-24 + 5 = -19$. Estimate: she went down more than up, so she should end deeper than $-12$ ✓.

blocks.html: Using a multiplying rule in an adding step, such as reading $-2 - 3$ as "two negatives make a positive." Name each operation before you use a rule: adding and subtracting are moves; multiplying and dividing use the sign rules for products.
